records.title: Trusted Records
records.subtitle: Every major event in this community — tokens granted, votes decided, rules changed — is archived here in public and sealed so no one can alter it; and any move that steps past the budget or voting rules is refused by the ledger on the spot.

write.title: Write it down
write.desc: Who did what, and how much they earned — every event is entered into the community ledger.

stamp.title: Seal it
stamp.desc: Each record gets a unique “digital fingerprint”, filed and sealed on a public ledger.

lock.title: Locked forever
lock.desc: Once sealed, no one — including us — can quietly rewrite history.

explainer.whyToggle: Why can you trust this page?
explainer.why1: A blockchain is like a notary office shared by the whole world: once a file goes in, it can never be edited or destroyed. We store each record's digital fingerprint on the Injective blockchain.
explainer.why2: Change even a single character of a record and its fingerprint becomes completely different. So as long as a record matches its on-chain fingerprint, it has provably never been touched since it was sealed.
explainer.why3: Only fingerprints and numbers go on-chain — never names, emails, or any personal information. Curious? Every record has a “Technical details” section so you can check the public ledger yourself.

guardian.title: The ledger blocks overreach on the spot
guardian.intro: This public ledger doesn't just stamp records — it's a strict rule-keeper. Even an admin who steps past the budget and governance rules the community set gets turned away on the spot. What proves its worth isn't a successful grant — it's an over-privileged attempt stopped at the door.

overMint.attempt: An admin tries to grant an insider more than the per-member cap in one go.
overMint.reason: The cap is hard-coded in the contract. Without a community vote to authorize it, the excess simply cannot be issued.

secretRule.attempt: Someone tries to quietly change monthly issuance from 5% to 8% without a vote.
secretRule.reason: There's only one path to change a rule: propose it, pass a community vote, and it takes effect next month. No way around it.

voteStuffing.attempt: Just before a vote closes, an admin grants supporters extra tokens to swing the result.
voteStuffing.reason: Each vote's weight is frozen at the moment the proposal opened. Tokens minted afterward can't affect that vote.

voteForYou.attempt: The YouFen platform tries to cast a vote on your behalf.
voteForYou.reason: Only the private key in your own hands can sign your vote. YouFen just sponsors the fee and relays your vote on-chain — it never holds your key.

guardian.boundary: The ledger guarantees power can't be over-issued: budgets, caps, and voting rules are unbypassable. It does not judge for the community whether a contribution is real or worthy — that always stays the community's call.
guardian.exitTitle: The community can leave with its ledger
guardian.exit: Every balance, grant, and vote lives on the public ledger. Even if YouFen shut down tomorrow, the community could still read its full history straight from the chain — no dependence on our database.

guide.s2: ② The status field should say Success;
guide.s3: ③ The timestamp should match the “sealed at” time above.
